proof:
An interior point of $K$ gives $\tau>0$ by summing its three strict lower support inequalities. The affine coordinates $\lambda_i$ sum to one, have minimum zero on $K$, and identify the aligned enclosure with the standard probability triangle. Using $\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ as coordinates, the physical inverse has determinant $\tau^2$, so its area is $\tau^2/2$.

The exact true-facet erosion theorem applies to the reference triangle $K$ without a matched-support hypothesis for its enclosure identity. At scale one its enclosures in original coordinates can be written $A\subseteq p+(2-\rho)K$ and $B\subseteq -p+\rho K$ by absorbing the reference centroid in the translation. Define $c_i=[v_i\cdot p+(\rho-1)t_i]/\tau$ and $d_i=(1+t_i)/\tau$. The two scalar enclosure ranges are contained in $c_i+(2-\rho)\lambda_i(K)$ and $-c_i+\rho\lambda_i(K)$, respectively. A point of $A$ below its proper cut has $\lambda_i<2\lambda_i(y)-d_i$, so $c_i+d_i<2\lambda_i(y)$. Summing and using $\sum_i c_i=\rho-1$ and $\sum_i d_i=1+3/\tau$ gives $\rho<2-3/\tau\le1$. This also gives $\tau>3/2$ and $b\le\rho^2k<k$.

In the enclosing homothet $-p+\rho K$, coordinate $\lambda_i$ has width $\rho m_i$ and maximum $\rho m_i-c_i$. Restriction to $T$ imposes $\lambda_i\le d_i$ on $B$. The enclosing maximum exceeds $d_i$ by more than $\rho m_i-2\lambda_i(y)$. When the latter is positive, a homothet about a maximizing point, of ratio equal to the actual excess divided by the width, lies in the removed cap. Its area is the ratio squared times $\rho^2 k$. The threshold is above the enclosing minimum because $B$ has positive area. When the latter lower bound on the excess is nonpositive, use $b\le\rho^2k$. This proves $b/k\le\rho^2-(\rho-2r_i)_+^2$. The right side as a function of $\rho\ge0$ strictly increases since it is $\rho^2$ before the hinge and has derivative $4r_i>0$ after it. Evaluation at one gives the strict placement inequality. This argument uses the actual offsets even if an individual $t_i$ is negative.

The mass assumptions give $b/k>32/33$, hence $r_i>(1-1/\sqrt{33})/2>41/100$ for all $i$. For a fixed $i$ the three vertex values of $\lambda_i$ are $0,u,m_i$ with $0\le u\le m_i$. Put $t=u/m_i$. The centroid threshold is $(u+m_i)/3$. If $\lambda_i(y)$ were at most this threshold, $r_i>41/100$ would imply $t>23/100$. By the two triangular tip formulas, the centroid cap has relative area $(2-t)^2/[9(1-t)]$ for $0\le t\le1/2$, and $1-(1+t)^2/(9t)$ for $1/2\le t\le1$. The first increases on its interval by differentiation. The second is at least $1/2$, since $2(1+t)^2\le9t$ there. Thus $t>23/100$ forces $q_i/k\ge31329/69300>65/144$. If all the cap areas satisfied the proposed ceiling, every $\lambda_i(y)$ would strictly exceed its centroid value, contradicting their unit sum.

For the common-budget statement, the displayed traces are from actual ambient halfspaces because their levels are affine in the base. Their $B$ traces carry zero planar area since $B\subseteq T$, so $q_i\le Q$. The middle traces cover the centroid by balance of the $v_i$, and their centroid-tail formula just derived is at least $4/9$ for every $t\in[0,1]$. Thus $Q\ge4k/9$. If $Q\le2(a+k+b)/9$, it follows that $k\le a+b$. We already have $b<k$ and $a<b/32$, so $q_i/k\le Q/k\le 2(1+a/k+b/k)/9<65/144$ for every $i$. This contradicts the previous conclusion.

statement:
In $\mathbb R^2$ put $v_1=(1,0)$, $v_2=(0,1)$, $v_3=(-1,-1)$ and $T=\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1\ \forall i\}$. Let $K$ be a triangle, and $A,B$ convex bodies with $B\subseteq T$ and $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Suppose for one $y$ all three lines $v_i\cdot x=2v_i\cdot y-1$ meet $\operatorname{int}A$. Write $a=|A|$, $k=|K|$, and $b=|B|$. Assume $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, and set $t_i=h_K(-v_i)$, $\tau=\sum_i t_i\le3$. The actual aligned enclosing triangle $\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge-t_i\}$ has area $\tau^2/2$. Write $\lambda_i(x)=(v_i\cdot x+t_i)/\tau$, $m_i=\max_K\lambda_i$, and $r_i=\lambda_i(y)/m_i>0$. The actual true-facet $B$-enclosure scale $\rho$ satisfies
$$
0<\rho<2-3/\tau\le1,\qquad
b/k\le \rho^2-(\rho-2r_i)_+^2<1-(1-2r_i)_+^2\quad\text{for every }i .
$$
In particular $\tau>3/2$ and $b<k$. If $a<b/32$ and $k\le a+b$, then every $r_i>(1-1/\sqrt{33})/2>41/100$, and the three middle cap areas $q_i=|K\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge v_i\cdot y\}|$ cannot all be at most $65k/144$.

On the three measured fibers $A,K,B$ at $-1,0,1$, if the actual ambient caps with these $A,K$ thresholds and with $B$ thresholds $1$ have equal mass $Q$ and $a<b/32$, then $Q>2(a+k+b)/9$. This last conclusion does not require a separate assumption $k\le a+b$.
title: True-facet triangle placement and cap budgets with unequal support offsets
